text:
The evidence can't tell you whether the removal was authorized. The tool explicitly says it does not establish legality, cause, responsible actor, or any compliance finding.

What it does show is that about 0.7 ha of tree-cover loss (1.2% of the 58.1 ha property) was mapped in 2023 and corroborated. A later year was observed, and the JRC 2020 map agrees the area was forest. The MGAP 2021 map classes 0.4 ha of the affected area as planted eucalyptus and 0.3 ha as outside mapped forest, with no native forest. That is only territorial context. It suggests plantation harvest may be possible, but it does not confirm a cause. A further 0.4 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

To answer the authorization question, you would need permits or harvest authorizations from the Uruguayan forestry authority, plus the landowner's records.
